title: A guarantor's liability - how far does it actually extend
p1:
Signing as a guarantor may feel like a simple favour. But what happens when the borrower stops paying? Many people discover the answer only after receiving a legal notice.

A common belief is that a guarantor is only a backup option. The reality can be very different.
p2:
A guarantor can become responsible for the debt if the borrower fails to meet the obligation. In many cases, the lender does not always need to exhaust every option against the borrower before approaching the guarantor.

The surprising part? Being a guarantor is not just giving a reference or showing support. It can create a legally enforceable responsibility.
p3:
The extent of liability usually depends on the terms of the guarantee agreement. It may cover the full amount owed, interest, and certain additional costs if mentioned in the agreement.

Before signing, always read what you are agreeing to. A few minutes of careful review can prevent years of financial stress.
conclusion: Would you sign as a guarantor for a close friend or family member? What factors would make you say yes or no?
